sources.title: Cameroon Humanitarian Situation Report No. 4 (End of Year), 31 December 2025
sources.temporal_coverage: Humanitarian events and UNICEF/partner response during 1 January-31 December 2025.
sources.methodology: UNICEF annual situation monitoring and partner-reported humanitarian results.
sources.limitations: Operational report, not an independent causal evaluation or representative coverage estimate.

sources.title: The situation in Central Africa and the activities of the United Nations Regional Office for Central Africa: Report of the Secretary-General (S/2026/445)
sources.temporal_coverage: Regional conditions and events from December 2025 through 15 March 2026; report dated 29 May 2026.
sources.methodology: Secretary-General regional reporting drawing on UN and cited partner sources, including ACLED and the regional climate centre.
sources.limitations: Climate conditions are described at subregional scale; the report does not attribute the Cameroon clash to climate.

claims.paraphrase: UNICEF says rainy-season flooding, particularly in Far North, damaged homes, schools, health and WASH facilities, isolated communities and heightened disease risk; conflict, displacement and recurrent floods converged nationally in 2025.
claims.limitations: The report gives no flood-attributable share of displacement or damage and does not identify all affected localities.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNICEF describes recurrent flooding alongside conflict and displacement as converging humanitarian pressures, not as a quantified causal link.

claims.locator: PDF p. 2, security and access update
claims.paraphrase: In North-West and South-West, UNICEF records 269 access constraints in 2025; insecurity, lockdowns and administrative impediments restricted humanitarian operations, while a five-week lockdown disrupted livelihoods and market access.
claims.limitations: The report does not quantify effects on climate-adaptation delivery.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNICEF states that insecurity and lockdowns constrained access and disrupted livelihoods.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 1-2, response highlights and funding overview
claims.paraphrase: Despite access and funding constraints, UNICEF reports community-based delivery and youth engagement, 80,000 feedback records, and anticipatory cash transfers to 2,800 households.
claims.limitations: Reported outputs do not establish durable resilience, equitable coverage or impact.

claims.paraphrase: The report describes Central African inland areas with below-normal rainfall, increasing pressure on water and pasture and affecting rain-fed and pastoral livelihoods; it separately records regional farmer-herder clashes.
institutions: United Nations Regional Office for Central Africa
Climate Application and Forecasting Centre of Central Africa
claims.limitations: Regional climate conditions are not disaggregated to Cameroon; report does not attribute the listed clashes to climate.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report frames climate and ecological pressures in its regional-stability discussion of farmer-herder dynamics, but makes no event-specific climate attribution.

claims.paraphrase: The Secretary-General reports that January 2026 violence in Logone-et-Chari, Far North, following livestock crop damage left nine people dead; the report does not attribute this clash to climate.
claims.limitations: The report identifies crop damage by livestock as preceding the violence, not climate as its cause.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report links the local violence to livestock-related crop damage, while leaving any climate connection unstated.

access_audit.notes: Downloaded and read the complete 17-page end-year report; claims use the situation overview, security/access update and response highlights.
Downloaded and read the 15-page Secretary-General report; climate and farmer-herder discussion is regional and does not establish climate causation for the Cameroon incident.
World Bank Climate Risk Country Profile (2025) direct PDF returned HTTP 403; PreventionWeb metadata was checked but no claim uses the profile.

search_audit.query: Cameroon 2025 flood impact Far North named regions climate humanitarian vulnerability report
search_audit.outcome: UNICEF's full 2025 report identifies flood damage particularly in Far North and separately reports multi-region conflict emergencies; it does not disaggregate every affected flood locality.

search_audit.query: Cameroon climate rainfall water pasture farmer herder conflict mediator official report
search_audit.outcome: The UN regional report states below-normal rainfall increased pressure on water and pasture and affected rural livelihoods; it discusses farmer-herder clashes in the same regional-stability section but does not attribute the Cameroon clash to climate.

search_audit.query: Cameroon conflict lockdown insecurity effect humanitarian access service delivery 2025 UNICEF
search_audit.outcome: UNICEF documents access constraints, lockdowns and insecurity restricting humanitarian operations and livelihoods in North-West and South-West; it does not quantify effects on climate-adaptation delivery.

search_audit.query: Cameroon anticipatory cash community-based humanitarian resilience response outputs 2025
search_audit.outcome: UNICEF reports community-based delivery, youth engagement, feedback records and anticipatory cash transfers; these operational outputs are not evaluated for durability or resilience impact.

gaps: The UNICEF report does not disaggregate all flood damage and displacement by named locality or estimate climate-attributable shares.
The Secretary-General's climate summary is regional; its Logone-et-Chari account links violence to livestock crop damage, not to climate conditions.
The World Bank 2025 Climate Risk Country Profile PDF returned HTTP 403 and was not used to support claims.
UNICEF operational delivery figures are not independent measures of coverage, durable resilience or causal impact.
